Building a Reflex ​

A reflex turns an event into work. This guide builds three, from trivial to load-bearing.

Reflex 1 — tell me when a run fails ​

json
{
  "name": "Notify on failed run",
  "enabled": true,
  "source": "run",
  "type": "run.failed",
  "match": { "field": "runId", "op": "exists" },
  "action": { "kind": "notify" },
  "brief": "Run \"{{actor}}\" failed. Last activity: {{payload.lastActivity}}"
}

source + type do the real filtering; the match tree here is just a guard that the payload is well-formed.

Reflex 2 — auto-triage a failing CI webhook ​

Assume an inbound webhook normalises GitHub check runs into source: 'github', type: 'check_run.completed'.

json
{
  "name": "Triage failing CI on master",
  "enabled": true,
  "source": "github",
  "type": "check_run.completed",
  "match": {
    "all": [
      { "field": "conclusion", "op": "eq", "value": "failure" },
      { "field": "branch", "op": "eq", "value": "master" },
      { "not": { "field": "repo", "op": "in", "value": ["sandbox", "scratch"] } }
    ]
  },
  "action": { "kind": "startRun" },
  "project": "my-app",
  "brief": "CI failed on master for {{payload.repo}} ({{payload.checkName}}). Investigate in ask mode first: find the failing test and the commit that introduced it. Do not push anything.",
  "cooldownSec": 900,
  "dedupKey": "{{payload.repo}}:{{payload.sha}}",
  "requireApproval": true
}

What each control is doing:

  • cooldownSec: 900 — a flapping check cannot start a run every 30 seconds.
  • dedupKey — the same repo+SHA within the TTL window is skipped, so three failing checks on one commit produce one run, not three.
  • requireApproval: true — the fire parks as a PendingReflexFire with a summary of what will happen. Nothing runs until you approve.
  • project — scopes the fired run so PRIME does not have to guess the target.
  • The brief says "ask mode first" and "do not push" — a reflex-started run has no human in the loop at the moment it starts. Write the brief for that.

Reflex 3 — chain follow-up work off a finished run ​

json
{
  "name": "Ship note after a release run",
  "enabled": true,
  "source": "run",
  "type": "run.finished",
  "match": {
    "all": [
      { "field": "title", "op": "matchesI", "value": "^release" },
      { "field": "project", "op": "eq", "value": "my-app" }
    ]
  },
  "action": { "kind": "callAgent", "agent": "comms" },
  "brief": "Run \"{{actor}}\" finished. Draft a customer-facing release note from its summary. Do not send it.",
  "maxFires": 50
}

callAgent hands the work to a custom agent rather than opening a run. Use startRun when the follow-up needs a plan and a branch; callAgent when it is one bounded task.

To fan further, use { "kind": "emitEvent", ... } — the bus carries a depth on chained events and caps it, so a cycle terminates instead of running away.

The changed operator ​

json
{ "field": "subscription.plan", "op": "changed" }

changed compares against the last value this reflex saw for that field. A first sighting counts as changed. It is the only stateful operator, and it is the right tool for "tell me when this number moves" — do not simulate it with neq against a constant.

Debugging: why didn't it fire? ​

Work down this list in order:

  1. Did the event arrive? The recent-events feed shows everything on the bus with a matched count. No event → the producer is the problem, not the reflex.
  2. Did it match? An event present with matched: 0 means your source/type or your match tree is wrong. Note that an invalid regex in matches fails closed.
  3. Was it skipped? The fire log records skipped with a reason — cooldown, dedup key, or maxFires reached.
  4. Is it parked? Status pending means requireApproval is on and it is waiting for you.
  5. Did it error? lastError on the reflex carries the reason.

Safety defaults worth keeping ​

  • Turn on requireApproval for anything that writes, until you have watched it fire a few times.
  • Always set a dedupKey when the source can emit duplicates. Most webhooks can.
  • Set maxFires on anything experimental — an auto-disable is much nicer than a bill.
  • Remember the fire acts as the reflex's creator: their budget and permissions.
